memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "A people that you do not know will eat what your land and labour produce, and you will have nothing but cruel oppression all your days. The sights you see will drive you mad... The Lord will afflict your knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be cured, spreading from the soles of your feet to the top of your head." — Deut 28:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The suffering described here is relentless — oppression all one's days, sights that drive a person mad, incurable affliction from head to toe. There is no relief in the picture, no corner untouched. This is the full weight of covenant judgment spelled out without any softening. It is meant to be unbearable to read, because it reflects the unbearable reality of a people wholly cut off from God's protecting hand.

Why does God set such stark warnings before His people? Because He loves them enough to tell them the truth. A God who only ever spoke of blessing, while hiding the real dangers of rebellion, would not be kind — He would be deceiving. The severity of the warning matches the severity of the danger.

We can be thankful that those in Christ are not under this covenant of curses. But we should let the passage do its sobering work: it shows us that sin, left to its own end, leads to ruin, and that we all need rescue.

And here is where our eyes lift to Jesus once more. The "cruel oppression" and unbearable affliction pictured here fell, in a deeper way, upon Him at the cross. He bore our griefs and carried our sorrows (Isa 53:4). What we could never survive, He endured in our place, so that we could be set free. The darkness of the warning is swallowed up in the light of His rescue.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I let God's warnings sober me and drive me to Christ?
2. How does Christ bearing our sorrows change how I read these hard verses?
3. Am I grateful for the rescue Jesus provides from what sin deserves?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Jesus bore the affliction I could never survive. Let Your warnings keep me humble and dependent, and let Your rescue fill me with gratitude. Amen.
